title: Every symbol belongs to one alphabet

statements.says: Studio's symbols serve three jobs, each its own alphabet: Identity names a page, Condition says how a part is doing, and Cause says what set a Skill off.
A symbol belongs to one alphabet and may be reused only inside it.
A test reads every table of symbols and fails when a symbol crosses alphabets.
A folder may name its own things, but it may not take a symbol the screen has already given away.
The pages gave way in all three clashes.
The page symbols are now a named table where they were five bare arguments inside a builder call.
The page symbols read ⌂ Home, ▦ Watch, ✎ Author, ✓ Test and ↑ Publish.
Every table names the alphabet it belongs to.
A word that never leaves its folder and never reaches the screen is not covered, and is the folder's own business.
Eight feature folders each kept their own table of symbols and none knew about the others, so six symbols came to mean two things at once.
No single ticket could see the clash; it showed only once Home put a page's symbol and a Health Lamp on one screen.
● was Watch in cyan and a working part in green, told apart by colour alone.
◈ was both Home and "Given to an agent", and ✦ was both Author and "Claude chose it".
Reuse inside one alphabet is what a reader wants: ✕ means broken, missing, unreachable and unlinked in four places, and says the same thing every time.
The pages gave way because a page symbol is only a label, while a filled dot is a lit lamp and a sparkle is Claude choosing.
Every table names its alphabet so the test has something to read.
One shared table of symbols was rejected, because it would pull pages, health, provenance and telemetry into a dependency none of them otherwise needs, so that four folders could share a constant.
Failing on any repeat was rejected, because ✕ would have to change in three of its four homes and the screen would lose a symbol that is doing its job.
